title: High-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells enabled by multifunctional titanium oxynitride recombination layers - Nature Energy
gist: A Soochow University-led team replaces the indium-containing transparent conductive oxide in monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems with titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy), reporting 33.3% power conversion efficiency on 1.0-cm2 devices and 30.6% on industrial-size 207.87 cm2 tandems with improved operational stability. The record is a Nature Energy abstract/landing page, so the hard content is the efficiency pair, the indium-free mechanism claim (vertical recombination, suppressed lateral leakage, tridentate SAM anchoring) and an author list stacked with Chinese PV manufacturers.

insights.claim: Titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy) can serve as the recombination layer in monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, removing indium from the interconnection stack entirely.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Indium is the supply-constrained input in tandem PV bill-of-materials; a credible indium-free interconnection layer removes a hard scaling ceiling and is bearish for indium-demand narratives tied to tandem buildout.
insights.quote: we show that titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy) can serve as a multifunctional, indium-free recombination layer that reconciles these competing requirements
insights.locator: Abstract — 'Here we show that titanium oxynitride'

insights.claim: The two incumbent recombination-layer options each carry a distinct penalty: indium-containing transparent conductive oxides raise cost and sustainability concerns, while silicon-based tunnel junctions suffer parasitic optical losses.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: This is the trade-off map for the whole interconnection-layer subsector — any new entrant must be scored on cost/sustainability versus parasitic absorption, not on efficiency alone.
insights.quote: Existing indium-containing transparent conductive oxides raise concerns regarding cost and sustainability, whereas silicon-based tunnel junctions suffer from parasitic optical losses.

insights.claim: The recombination layer, not the absorber, is identified as the component constraining performance, stability and scalability of monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Redirects the bottleneck away from perovskite absorber chemistry toward the interconnection stack — that is where the next round of tandem-PV differentiation and IP will be fought.
insights.quote: their performance, stability and scalability are constrained by the recombination layer, which needs to simultaneously enable efficient charge recombination, high optical transparency and robust interfacial chemistry

themes.theme: Efficiency at lab versus industrial area

insights.claim: The TiOxNy-based tandem reaches 33.3% power conversion efficiency on a 1.0-cm2 device, placing it in the top tier of reported perovskite/silicon tandem results.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: 33.3% at 1 cm2 is the number to benchmark rival indium-free interconnection approaches against.
insights.quote: we achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 33.3% for 1.0-cm2 devices and 30.6% for industrial-size (207.87 cm2) tandems, with enhanced operational stability

insights.claim: The same TiOxNy stack delivers 30.6% efficiency at an industrial size of 207.87 cm2, meaning only ~2.7 percentage points are lost scaling area by roughly 200x.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Area scaling is where most perovskite tandem results collapse; a sub-3-point drop to full wafer scale is the single most commercially relevant datum in this paper.
insights.locator: Abstract — results sentence; Fig. 2 'Performance of industrial-size tandems with TiOxNy'

themes.theme: Why TiOxNy works: three functions in one film

insights.claim: Conductive TiOxNy performs three jobs at once in the tandem interconnection: it enables efficient vertical carrier recombination, suppresses lateral leakage, and provides anchoring sites for self-assembled monolayers.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Multifunctionality is what lets one deposition step replace several — a direct capex and yield argument for equipment vendors selling into tandem lines.
insights.quote: Conductive TiOxNy enables efficient vertical carrier recombination, suppresses lateral leakage and provides anchoring sites for self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) via a tridentate binding configuration.

insights.claim: The SAM binds to TiOxNy through a tridentate binding configuration, a specific three-point anchoring geometry the authors credit for the interfacial robustness.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: SAM detachment is a known degradation pathway in p-i-n perovskite cells; a substrate that binds SAMs more strongly is a differentiated, patentable stability lever.
insights.locator: Abstract — mechanism sentence; Fig. 4 'SAM adsorption on TiOxNy'

insights.claim: The mechanistic case is built with DFT calculations run in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package plus SCAPS-1D device simulation, alongside GIWAXS measurements of perovskite growth on the TiOxNy/SAM stack.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The combination of first-principles binding analysis with device-level simulation is the evidentiary standard now expected for interface claims in tandem PV — useful for triaging weaker competing papers.
insights.quote: Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) for the DFT calculations is available at https://www.vasp.at/.

insights.claim: Employees of three Chinese PV manufacturers — Suzhou Maxwell Technologies, Wuxi EliTe Solar and Hangzhou Zhongneng Photoelectricity Technology — are co-authors and declare competing interests, with Maxwell staff fabricating the SHJ bottom cells and EliTe staff fabricating the tandem mini-module.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Equipment and cell makers doing the actual device fabrication in an academic paper is the strongest available tell that this is being staged for a production line, not left as a lab curiosity — watch these three names for tandem-line announcements.
insights.quote: J. Zhou, C.Y., S.Y. and X.C. are employees of Suzhou Maxwell Technologies Co. Ltd. J. Yu, Y.Z., Y.W. and J. Zhu are employees of Wuxi EliTe Solar Co. Ltd.

insights.claim: The work is anchored by a Joint R&D Center of Suzhou National Laboratory, Kunshan GCL Optoelectronic Material and Soochow University, embedding the tandem effort inside China's national-lab and polysilicon-supply-chain apparatus.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: GCL's involvement links tandem interconnection R&D directly to an incumbent silicon-materials supplier — a route by which existing PV capex gets upgraded rather than displaced.
insights.quote: We acknowledge the Joint R&D Center of Suzhou National Laboratory, Kunshan GCL Optoelectronic Material Co., Ltd., and Soochow University.
